newsitem.title: USA: Judges propose smaller CSW rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Judges propose smaller CSW rate rise.

text.p: Central and South West Corp said Wednesday administrative law judges for the State Office of Administrative Hearings proposed its Central Power and Light Co receive a $7.2 million annual rate increase.
The recommendation comes in a Proposal for Decision issued Tuesday on the utility's request for $71 million in rate relief, which has been pending since November 1995.

A factor contributing significantly to the difference between the retail base rate increase CPL requested and the law judges' proposal included their recommendation of a 10.9 percent return on equity, CSW said.
Reducing the return from CPL's requested 12.25 percent resulted in a reduction of $30 million in the recommended base rate increase, the company said.

Another factor involves the capitalized costs associated with the South Texas Nuclear Project. The judges suggested rejection of a request to change recovery of deferred accounting costs to a straight-line recovery from a mortgage methodology. The judges formed that opinion although the Public Utility Commission of Texas staff had supported CPL's request for a change, the utility said.
The judges also recommended that CPL's current depreciation rates be decreased by $8.8 million a year.
The $7.2 million rate increase would be the net result of a recommended base rate reduction of $5.2 million plus increased revenues collected through two surcharges.
-- A $10.3 million reduction in kilowatt-hour-related revenues,
-- An increase of $5.1 million in miscellaneous revenues (customer connect charges, insufficient check charges and other fees),
-- A $4.3 million annual surcharge applied over three years to recover rate case expenses, and
-- Annual recovery of $8.1 million for demand-side management expenditures through a separate surcharge.
"Obviously, we are extremely disappointed with the judges' proposal," said CSW chief executive Dick Brooks.

"The proposal ignores the opportunity to take any innovative steps to better prepare CPL for a competitive future. In fact, the proposal moves in the opposite direction by reducing the depreciation primarily for CPL's generating plants."
He added, "We are currently analyzing the effect these recommendations will have on 1996 earnings and anticipate releasing preliminary earnings on Thursday."

CSW said the requested increase of $71 million was put into effect under bond in May 1996. The difference between the bonded rates collected and the rate levels ultimately approved by regulators in March is subject to refund to customers with interest.
